alias.desc: Renames the output expression column key.

cast.desc: Coerces the column data type to another type.

debug.desc: Prints the current evaluation intermediate array to console for debugging.

all.desc: Creates an expression targeting all columns in the DataFrame.
all.returns: {ColumnExpr<any>} A column expression targeting all columns.

coalesce.desc: Returns the first non-null value among the specified expressions.

params.name: exprs
params.desc: The list of expressions or columns to coalesce.

coalesce.returns: {ColumnExpr<any>} A column expression resolving to the first non-null value.

element.desc: Creates an expression referencing the current element(s) of an array during evaluation. Primarily used inside array operations like `filter`, `map`, or `eval`.
element.returns: {ColumnExpr<T>} A column expression referencing the array element.

exclude.desc: Creates an expression targeting all columns except the specified ones.

params.name: columns
params.desc: The name or names of columns to exclude.

exclude.returns: {ColumnExpr<any>} A column expression targeting all columns except the specified ones.

implode.desc: Aggregates values of a column into a list within each group.

params.name: column
params.desc: The column or expression to implode.

implode.returns: {ColumnExpr<any>} A column expression representing the list of values.

lit.desc: Creates a literal column expression that repeats the given value for all rows.

params.name: value
params.desc: The literal value (number, string, boolean, etc.).

params.name: [options]
params.desc: Configuration options.

params.name: [options.dtype]
params.desc: The data type to allocate for the literal values.

params.name: [options.name]
params.desc: The name of the output column.

lit.returns: {ColumnExpr<any>} A column expression with the literal value.

seq_range.desc: Creates a column expression that generates a range of values. If mode is "cumulative" (default) or "independent", it generates a sequence. If mode is "constant", it repeats the given value.

params.name: value
params.desc: The initial value to start the sequence or the constant value to repeat.

params.name: [options]
params.desc: Configuration options.

params.name: [options.n]
params.desc: The number of values to generate. Defaults to the slice/DataFrame height.

params.name: [options.dtype]
params.desc: The registered data type to coerce/allocate for the generated sequence.

params.name: [options.name]
params.desc: The name of the output column.

params.name: [options.mode]
params.desc: The sequence generation mode ("constant", "cumulative", or "independent").

params.name: [options.step]
params.desc: The step value or function to compute the step at each row.

params.name: [options.strict]
params.desc: If true, throws an error if the generated sequence height does not match the target height.

params.name: [options.pad]
params.desc: In non-strict mode, pads the sequence with `padValue` if it is shorter than target range.

params.name: [options.truncate]
params.desc: In non-strict mode, truncates the sequence if it exceeds target range.

params.name: [options.padValue]
params.desc: The value to use for padding in non-strict mode.

params.name: [options.startIndex]
params.desc: The starting index in the DataFrame to insert the sequence.

params.name: [options.endIndex]
params.desc: The ending index in the DataFrame to insert the sequence.

seq_range.returns: {ColumnExpr<any>} A column expression generating the sequence.

struct.desc: Packages multiple expressions into a structured object column.

params.name: fields
params.desc: An array of expressions, a record of field names to expressions, or a single expression.

params.name: moreFields
params.desc: Additional fields when a single expression is passed as the first parameter.

struct.returns: {ColumnExpr<any>} A column expression packaging the specified fields.
struct.signature:
$df.struct(
  fields: IntoExpr[] | Record<string, IntoExpr> | IntoExpr,
  ...moreFields: IntoExpr[]
): ColumnExpr<any>

when.desc: Provides conditional branch evaluations inside column expressions.

params.name: predicate
params.desc: The boolean condition or expression.

when.returns: {When} A When object builder to chain `.then()` and `.otherwise()`/`.when()`.

all.desc: Aggregation: Returns true if all values in the group are truthy.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A", "B"], val: [true, true, false] })
>>> df.group_by("group").agg($df.col("val").all().alias("all_true"))
shape: (2, 2)
┌───────┬──────────┐
│ group │ all_true │
├───────┼──────────┤
│ "A"   │ true     │
│ "B"   │ false    │
└───────┴──────────┘

all_null.desc: Aggregation: Checks if all values in the group are null.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A"], val: [null, null] })
>>> df.group_by("group").agg($df.col("val").all_null().alias("is_null"))
shape: (1, 2)
┌───────┬─────────┐
│ group │ is_null │
├───────┼─────────┤
│ "A"   │ true    │
└───────┴─────────┘

any.desc: Aggregation: Checks if any value in the group is truthy.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A", "B"], val: [true, false, false] })
>>> df.group_by("group").agg($df.col("val").any().alias("any_true"))
shape: (2, 2)
┌───────┬──────────┐
│ group │ any_true │
├───────┼──────────┤
│ "A"   │ true     │
│ "B"   │ false    │
└───────┴──────────┘

any_null.desc: Aggregation: Checks if any value in the group is null.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A"], val: [10, null] })
>>> df.group_by("group").agg($df.col("val").any_null().alias("has_null"))
shape: (1, 2)
┌───────┬──────────┐
│ group │ has_null │
├───────┼──────────┤
│ "A"   │ true     │
└───────┴──────────┘

avg.desc: Aggregation: Computes the arithmetic mean of the group.

corr.desc: Aggregation: Computes the Pearson correlation coefficient between two columns.

params.name: other
params.desc: The target column expression to correlate with.

count.desc: Aggregation: Returns the count of records inside the group.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A"], val: [10, null] })
>>> df.group_by("group").agg($df.col("val").count().alias("cnt"))
shape: (1, 2)
┌───────┬─────┐
│ group │ cnt │
├───────┼─────┤
│ "A"   │ 1   │
└───────┴─────┘

params.name: options
params.desc: Config flags including whether to count null values.

cov.desc: Aggregation: Computes the covariance between two columns.

params.name: other
params.desc: The target column expression to compute covariance with.

dot.desc: Aggregation: Computes the dot product with another column.

params.name: other
params.desc: The other column expression to compute the dot product with.

first.desc: Aggregation: Finds the first value in the group.

implode.desc: Aggregation: Combines all values in the group into a single array/list cell.

last.desc: Aggregation: Finds the last value in the group.

max.desc: Aggregation: Finds the maximum value in the group.

mean.desc: Aggregation: Computes the arithmetic mean of elements in the group.

min.desc: Aggregation: Finds the minimum value in the group.

mode.desc: Aggregation: Finds the statistical mode (most frequent value).

n_unique.desc: Aggregation: Computes number of unique elements.

params.name: options
params.desc: Uniqueness options.

null_count.desc: Aggregation: Counts the number of null or missing records.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ group: ["A", "A"], val: [10, null] })
>>> df.group_by("group").agg($df.col("val").null_count().alias("nulls"))
shape: (1, 2)
┌───────┬───────┐
│ group │ nulls │
├───────┼───────┤
│ "A"   │ 1     │
└───────┴───────┘

quantile.desc: Aggregation: Computes the specific quantile values (0.0 to 1.0).

params.name: q
params.desc: The quantile parameter value between 0.0 and 1.0.

spearman_corr.desc: Aggregation: Computes the Spearman rank correlation coefficient.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ x: [1, 2, 3], y: [5, 6, 7] })
>>> df.select($df.col("x").spearman_corr($df.col("y")).alias("spearman"))
shape: (1, 1)
┌──────────┐
│ spearman │
├──────────┤
│ 1        │
└──────────┘

params.name: other
params.desc: The other column expression to correlate with.

sum.desc: Aggregation: Computes the sum of elements in the group.

examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ val: [10, 20], weight: [1, 3] })
>>> df.select($df.col("val").w_avg($df.col("weight")).alias("w_mean"))
shape: (1, 1)
┌────────┐
│ w_mean │
├────────┤
│ 17.5   │
└────────┘

params.name: weights
params.desc: The weight values or column expression.

abs.desc: Computes the absolute value of the column values.

acos.desc: Computes the mathematical arccosine (inverse cosine) of the column values.

acosh.desc: Computes the hyperbolic arccosine of the column values.

add.desc: Adds a scalar value or another column expression.

params.name: val
params.desc: The number or column expression to add.

asin.desc: Computes the arcsine of the column values.

asinh.desc: Computes the hyperbolic arcsine of the column values.

atan.desc: Computes the arctangent of the column values.

atan2.desc: Computes the quadrant-aware arctangent of two values.

params.name: val
params.desc: The x denominator number or column expression.

atanh.desc: Computes the hyperbolic arctangent of the column values.

cbrt.desc: Computes the cube root of the column values.

ceil.desc: Rounds column values up to the nearest integer.

clip.desc: Clamps column values between lower and upper numeric thresholds.

params.name: lower
params.desc: The lower threshold value (default: null).

params.name: upper
params.desc: The upper threshold value (default: null).

clip.signature:
$df.col(<column_name>).clip(
  lower: number | null = null,
  upper: number | null = null
)

copysign.desc: Returns absolute value of expr with the sign of other.

params.name: val
params.desc: The sign source value or column expression.

cos.desc: Computes the cosine of the column values.

cosh.desc: Computes the hyperbolic cosine of the column values.

degrees.desc: Converts angles from radians to degrees.

div.desc: Divides column values by a scalar or another column expression.

params.name: val
params.desc: The denominator value or column expression.

exp.desc: Computes natural exponent (e^x) of the column values.

expm1.desc: Computes e^x - 1 for each element in the column.

floor.desc: Rounds column values down to the nearest integer.

floordiv.desc: Performs integer division floor(x / y) on column values.

params.name: val
params.desc: The divisor value or column expression.

hypot.desc: Computes the hypotenuse sqrt(x^2 + y^2) of two values.

params.name: val
params.desc: The other numeric value or column expression.

log.desc: Computes the logarithm of positive values with a specified base.

params.name: base
params.desc: The base of the logarithm (default: Math.E).

mod.desc: Computes modulo remainder (x % y) of column values.

params.name: val
params.desc: The divisor value or column expression.

mul.desc: Multiplies column values by a scalar or another column expression.

params.name: val
params.desc: The multiplier value or column expression.

pow.desc: Raises column values to the specified power.

params.name: val
params.desc: The exponent power value or column expression.

radians.desc: Converts angles from degrees to radians.

rand.desc: Fills sequence with pseudo-random generated floats or integers.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ index: [1, 2, 3] })
>>> df.with_columns($df.col("index").rand(42, { min: 1, max: 10, integer: true }).alias("random"))
shape: (3, 2)
┌───────┬────────┐
│ index │ random │
├───────┼────────┤
│ 1     │ 2      │
│ 2     │ 5      │
│ 3     │ 6      │
└───────┴────────┘

params.name: seed
params.desc: Optional seed to initialize the pseudo-random generator.

params.name: options
params.desc: Config options including min, max, and integer flag.

round.desc: Rounds values to a specific scale of decimal digits.

params.name: decimals
params.desc: Number of decimal places to round to (default: 0).

round_sig_figs.desc: Rounds values to a specific number of significant figures.

params.name: sig_figs
params.desc: Number of significant figures.

sign.desc: Returns sign indicator of column values (-1, 0, or 1).

sin.desc: Computes the sine of the column values.

sinh.desc: Computes the hyperbolic sine of the column values.

sqrt.desc: Computes the square root of non-negative column values.

sub.desc: Subtracts a scalar or another column expression.

params.name: val
params.desc: The value or column expression to subtract.

tan.desc: Computes the tangent of the column values.

tanh.desc: Computes the hyperbolic tangent of the column values.

trunc.desc: Truncates fractional digits of column values.

eq.desc: Boolean comparison: Returns true if column values match the specified value exactly.

ge.desc: Boolean comparison: Returns true if greater than or equal to argument.

params.name: val
params.desc: The value or column expression to compare against.

gt.desc: Boolean comparison: Returns true if column value is greater than argument.

params.name: val
params.desc: The value or column expression to compare against.

is_duplicated.desc: Checks if values occur more than once in the column.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2, 2] })
>>> df.with_columns($df.col("a").is_duplicated().alias("dup"))
shape: (3, 2)
┌───┬───────┐

│ 2 │ true  │

└───┴───────┘

>>> const df = $df.data({ a: ["", "hello", []] })
>>> df.with_columns($df.col("a").is_empty().alias("empty"))
shape: (3, 2)

>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1.5, Infinity, NaN] })
>>> df.with_columns($df.col("a").is_finite().alias("finite"))
shape: (3, 2)
┌──────────┬────────┐
│ a        │ finite │
├──────────┼────────┤
│ 1.5      │ true   │
│ Infinity │ false  │
│ NaN      │ false  │
└──────────┴────────┘

is_in.desc: Checks if column values are members of a specified array or list.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ category: ["toys", "books", "food"] })
>>> df.with_columns($df.col("category").is_in(["toys", "books"]).alias("in_list"))
shape: (3, 2)

├──────────┼─────────┤

│ "food"   │ false   │
└──────────┴─────────┘

params.desc: An array of candidate values or a single value to match against.

is_infinite.desc: Checks if values are positive or negative Infinity.

shape: (3, 2)
┌───────────┬───────┐
│ a         │ inf   │

│ 1.5       │ false │
│ Infinity  │ true  │
│ -Infinity │ true  │
└───────────┴───────┘

>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1.5, NaN] })
>>> df.with_columns($df.col("a").is_nan().alias("nan"))
shape: (2, 2)
┌─────┬───────┐
│ a   │ nan   │
├─────┼───────┤
│ 1.5 │ false │
│ NaN │ true  │
└─────┴───────┘

shape: (2, 2)
┌─────┬─────────┐
│ a   │ not_nan │
├─────┼─────────┤
│ 1.5 │ true    │
│ NaN │ false   │
└─────┴─────────┘

is_not_null.desc: Checks if column values are non-null and valid (not null, undefined, or missing).

│ alice@example.com │ true  │
│ null              │ false │
└───────────────────┴───────┘

is_null.desc: Checks if column values are null, undefined, or missing.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ email: ["alice@example.com", null] })

│ alice@example.com │ false   │
│ null              │ true    │
└───────────────────┴─────────┘

is_unique.desc: Checks if values occur exactly once in the column.
examples:
>>> const df = $df.data({ a: [1, 2, 2] })
>>> df.with_columns($df.col("a").is_unique().alias("uniq"))
shape: (3, 2)
┌───┬───────┐
│ a │ uniq  │
├───┼───────┤
│ 1 │ true  │
│ 2 │ false │
│ 2 │ false │
└───┴───────┘

lt.desc: Boolean comparison: Returns true if less than argument.

params.name: val
params.desc: The value or column expression to compare against.

DateTimeExprNamespace.desc:
**Implementation Notes**

_TimeUnit_: `Date` objects are always millisecond-based, so `timeUnit` is schema metadata only. Sub-millisecond precision (`us`, `ns`) cannot be stored; methods such as `microsecond()` and `nanosecond()` always scale from milliseconds. Migrating to raw `BigInt` arrays would be required for true sub-ms storage.

_Timezone enforcement_: `convert_time_zone` can only validate that the column is timezone-aware when `_castType` is explicitly set within the expression chain (e.g. after `cast_time_unit`). Enforcement against a column whose type is unknown at expression-build time requires schema-level checks in DataFrame operations.

cast_time_unit.desc: Casts the schema time unit of a Datetime column (`"ms"`, `"us"`, `"ns"`). This is a metadata-only operation — underlying millisecond Date timestamps are preserved.

params.name: unit
params.desc: Target time unit: `"ms"` (milliseconds), `"us"` (microseconds), or `"ns"` (nanoseconds).

century.desc: Extracts the 1-indexed century component (e.g. 21 for 2026) from a Datetime column.

convert_time_zone.desc: Converts a Datetime column to a different IANA timezone. Preserves the exact UTC epoch instant while changing the timezone label, affecting how local wall-clock component extractors (`hour()`, `day()`, etc.) and `strftime` interpret values. Requires the column to already be timezone-aware; use `replace({ timeZone })` to assign a timezone to a naive column first.

params.name: timeZone
params.desc: Target IANA timezone identifier (e.g. `"UTC"`, `"America/New_York"`, `"Europe/London"`).

date.desc: Extracts the Date object component from a Datetime column, truncating time to 00:00:00.000 UTC.

day.desc: Extracts the calendar day component (1-31) from a Datetime column.

params.name: timeZone
params.desc: Optional IANA timezone identifier. Defaults to the column timezone or UTC.

days_in_month.desc: Extracts the total number of days in the month (28-31) for each Datetime value.

params.name: timeZone
params.desc: Optional IANA timezone identifier. Defaults to the column timezone or UTC.

epoch.desc: Returns the epoch duration timestamp offset in the specified time resolution unit.

params.name: unit

params.name: timeZone
params.desc: Optional IANA timezone identifier. Defaults to the column timezone or UTC.

is_business_day.desc: Evaluates whether each Datetime value falls on a business day. Supports custom weekend day definitions and holiday arrays or timestamp sets.

params.name: options
params.desc: Business day rules and custom holiday configuration options.

join_asof.desc:
Performs an asof (as-of) join for inexact matching on ordered numeric or temporal key columns.

Similar to a left join, but instead of exact key equality, matches the nearest key row from the right DataFrame according to the selected `strategy` ("backward", "forward", or "nearest") and optional `tolerance`. Both DataFrames must be sorted in ascending order on their respective `on` / `leftOn` / `rightOn` join keys.

- `"backward"` — Matches the latest right row where `rightKey <= leftKey`. - `"forward"` — Matches the earliest right row where `rightKey >= leftKey`. - `"nearest"` — Matches the right row with the absolute nearest key value to `leftKey`.

df.join_asof({ other, on, leftOn, rightOn, by, leftBy, rightBy, strategy, tolerance, allow_exact_matches, suffixes, coalesce, check_sorted })
examples:
>>> const trades = new DataFrame([
...   { time: 1000, ticker: "AAPL", price: 150.0 },
...   { time: 1005, ticker: "AAPL", price: 150.5 },
...   { time: 1015, ticker: "AAPL", price: 151.0 }
... ]);
>>> const quotes = new DataFrame([
...   { time: 998, ticker: "AAPL", bid: 149.9 },
...   { time: 1004, ticker: "AAPL", bid: 150.4 },
...   { time: 1010, ticker: "AAPL", bid: 150.8 }
... ]);
>>> const joined = trades.join_asof({
...   other: quotes,
...   on: "time",
...   by: "ticker",
...   strategy: "backward"
... });
>>> joined
shape: (3, 4)
┌──────┬────────┬───────┬──────┐
│ time │ ticker │ price │ bid  │
├──────┼────────┼───────┼──────┤
│ 1000 │ AAPL   │ 150.0 │ 149.9│
│ 1005 │ AAPL   │ 150.5 │ 150.4│
│ 1015 │ AAPL   │ 151.0 │ 150.8│
└──────┴────────┴───────┴──────┘

concat.desc: Concatenates items vertically, horizontally, or diagonally.
examples:
// 1. Vertical Concatenation (default):
>>> const df1 = $df.data({ a: [1] })
>>> const df2 = $df.data({ a: [2] })
>>> $df.concat([df1, df2], { how: "vertical" })
shape: (2, 1)
┌───┐
│ a │
├───┤
│ 1 │
│ 2 │
└───┘

// 2. Horizontal Concatenation:
>>> const df1 = $df.data({ a: [1] })
>>> const df2 = $df.data({ b: [2] })
>>> $df.concat([df1, df2], { how: "horizontal" })
shape: (1, 2)
┌───┬───┐
│ a │ b │
├───┼───┤
│ 1 │ 2 │
└───┴───┘

// 3. Diagonal Concatenation (mismatched columns):
>>> const df1 = $df.data({ a: [1] })
>>> const df2 = $df.data({ b: [2] })
>>> $df.concat([df1, df2], { how: "diagonal" })
shape: (2, 2)
┌──────┬──────┐
│ a    │ b    │
├──────┼──────┤
│ 1    │ null │
│ null │ 2    │
└──────┴──────┘
